patch_resolves_note: The fixed original preserves the same nested-list source event in `__cil_resolve_perms()`, but its verifier only emits the protected permission-use event for the recursively reached inner datum (`map_perm_root.item_is_datum=1`, `map_perm_item_use.item_is_list=0`) and exits cleanly. The vulnerable original reaches that same protected event with `map_perm_root.item_is_datum=0` and `map_perm_item_use.item_is_list=1` on the outer nested-list pointer, so the missing datum-only guard is differentially confirmed on the original witness with no perturbation.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that consumes the witness fragment `cm1((mp1))` and stores the attacker-controlled class identifier used later to select the map-class verifier branch.

Root cause. In the map-class branch, the verifier only filters out operators and assumes every other permission-expression item is a `struct cil_perm`. Nested permission lists therefore bypass validation even though their `i->flavor` is `CIL_LIST`, not `CIL_DATUM`.

AddressSanitizer crash site. Evaluating this recursive-call argument list dereferences `cmp` as a `struct cil_perm` even though `cmp` actually points to a nested `struct cil_list`, producing the saved heap-buffer-overflow read.

nodes.state: At the cast site, `struct cil_perm *cmp = i->data` reinterprets a nested-list item as a permission object because the same event still sees `i->flavor == CIL_LIST`.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `map_perm_item_use.item_is_list == 1` at the line that assigns `cmp` from `i->data`.

nodes.state: The resolver preserves the witness's nested permission subexpression as a `CIL_LIST` item instead of flattening it to a permission datum before verification.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `resolved_nested_perm_list.stored_as_list == 1` when `sub_list` is appended back into the resolved permission list.

edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `map_perm_item_use.perm_ptr == map_perm_recursive_sink.perm_ptr`.
The vulnerable original trace records `map_perm_root.item_data_ptr == map_perm_item_use.perm_ptr`.
The vulnerable original trace records `resolved_nested_perm_list.sub_list_ptr == map_perm_root.item_data_ptr`.
